title: Place value up to one million

blocks.content: In our number system, where a digit sits decides how much it is worth. The same digit 5 can mean five, fifty, or five hundred — it all depends on its place.
Each place, from the right, is worth ten times the one before: ones, tens, hundreds, thousands, ten-thousands, hundred-thousands, millions.

steps: The 3 sits in the hundreds place.

blocks.prompt: In 5,308, the value of the digit 3 is ___.
blocks.explain: The 3 is in the hundreds place, so its value is 3 x 100 = 300.
blocks.rule: A digit's value is the digit multiplied by its place (ones, tens, hundreds, thousands...).

blocks.content: To name a digit's place, count the columns from the right: ones, tens, hundreds, then thousands.

blocks.question: In the number 6,245, the digit 2 is in which place?
blocks.explain: Counting from the right: 5 ones, 4 tens, 2 hundreds. So the 2 is in the hundreds place.
blocks.rule: Count the columns from the right to name a digit's place: ones, tens, hundreds, thousands.

blocks.content: Where a digit sits tells you its value. Count the places from the right and you can read any number up to a million. Let's practise!
